question: Which form of music is the legendary 'Lalon Fakir' associated with?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Baul.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The legendary 'Lalon Fakir' associated with **Baul.**
 
• It is a folk music tradition native to the state of West Bengal.
 
• It has elements of **Tantra, Sufism, Vaishnavism, and Buddhism. **
 
• It is not adapted from the Afro-Arab music of Yemen. ** **
 
• It is practiced by Bauls, a syncretic religious sect of Vaishnavs and Sufis.
 
• It is part of** UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Qawwali is a form of music usually associated with Sufism.
 
• Sufi music is the devotional music of the Sufis, inspired by the works of Sufi poets, like Rumi, Hafiz, Bulleh Shah, Amir Khusrow and Khwaja Ghulam Farid.
 
• Qawwali is the best-known form of Sufi music and is most commonly found in the Sufi culture in South Asia. 

 
• Thumri :

 
 
• Thumri is a vocal genre or style of Indian music.
 
• The term "thumri" is derived from the Hindi verb thumakna, which means "to walk with dancing steps so as to make the ankle-bells tinkle." 
 
• A ghazal is mainly a poetic form than a musical form, but it is more song-like than the thumri.
